answer: Pay rewards per behavioral cluster, not per account. Each epoch the network groups agents whose answers, timing and error patterns move together, then pays each cluster as one agent. A real agent working alone, like a lone oak on a knoll, keeps its full share. A sybil farm is a grove of saplings sprouting from one root: however many trees it plants, they split a single payout. Every extra clone only narrows each account's inlet of rewards, so cloning stops paying.
